sections.heading: C — Impairment and Trip Planning
sections.markdown:
## C — Impairment and Trip Planning

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Impaired driving ranks among the hardest-enforced road laws, and Iowa punishes alcohol and drug intoxication steeply [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Operating while intoxicated means a BAC of .08 or higher or any controlled substance aboard, proven by breath, urine, or blood tests [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Even a criminal-court acquittal still costs at least 180 days of driving privileges, and repeat offenses stretch revocations and sharpen criminal pain [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Holding an Iowa license signs you to field sobriety tests on officer demand under Iowa Code section 321J.6, binding visitors too [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Refusing the breathalyzer neither blocks conviction nor saves your license, and out-punishes failing with an automatic one-year revocation plus a minimum $1,250 fine [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Refusal convictions may add a mandatory substance-use class and evaluation or a self-paid ignition interlock [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Underage drivers hit OWI at .02 BAC, losing privileges at least 60 days, or at least 180 days past .08 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Offenders under 18 get no temporary restricted license during an OWI revocation [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Open alcohol belongs to no cabin occupant, though trunks may carry it, and cabin violations cost each driver and rider up to a $200 simple misdemeanor [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
Drowsy driving kills like drunk driving through slow reactions, lane weaving, road departures, and crash proneness [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
Mind warnings of drowsiness include daydreaming, forgotten miles, repeated yawns, eye rubbing, and a drooping head [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
Road warnings of drowsiness include lane drifting, tailgating, rumble-strip strikes, restlessness, and irritability, all cueing a break, a safe pullover, or a driver swap [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
Eighteen straight waking hours impair like a 0.08 percent BAC with matching crash risk [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
Plan every trip, familiar or far, around weather, construction, and crashes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Iowa 511 serves highway and interstate conditions at 511ia.org and through its free mobile app [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0038]

Misconceptions: refusing the test dodges punishment, yet refusal punishes harder than failure; drowsiness impairs like drunkenness rather than mere tiredness; an open bottle in the trunk stays legal while one in the cabin does not.

Mnemonic: eight means over for adults, two means over for teens; sleepy signs mean stop or swap; plan trips on five-eleven.

Glossary: operating while intoxicated (driving at or past the legal alcohol or drug limit); implied consent (license-holding as agreement to sobriety testing); ignition interlock (a car device gating starts on sobriety); rumble strip (a shoulder strip buzzing drifting tires).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every impairment and trip-planning rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
